Bar screens mechanically remove approximately 4 wet tons of large debris per month from the waste stream and grit chambers remove approximately 11 wet tons per month of grit from the waste stream.
Primary sedimentation: The main objective of primary sedimentation is to remove solids from the wastewater by gravity.
Tapia WRF uses the following process sequence: ... activated sludge biological treatment with nitrification and denitrification ...
Tapia WRF uses the following process sequence: ... secondary sedimentation, tertiary filtration, disinfection ...
Aluminum sulfate (alum) is added prior to filtration to enhance solids removal.
Inert media filtration: The filtration process is used to remove or reduce suspended or colloidal matter from a liquid stream, by passing the water through a bed of graded granular material.
Disinfection: Sodium hypochlorite and ammonia are added to the treated effluent prior to the filters to destroy bacteria, pathogens and viruses, and to minimize algal growth in the filters.
Prior to discharge, sodium bisulfite is added to the treated effluent to remove residual chlorine.

The return activated sludge (RAS), prior to returning to the secondary treatment system, undergoes reaeration treatment to facilitate nitrogen and phosphorus removal as well as to provide favorable conditions for the development of a facultative anaerobic biomass.

As of September 2009, Tapia WRF’s centrate undergoes treatment provided by the Centrate Treatment Unit (CTU)... consists of two 800,000 gallon tanks connected to pumps and blowers, consists of aeration, mixing, settling, and decanting.
Prior to 1993 the principal solids treatment route was aerobic digestion at Tapia WRF and land application at the Rancho Las Virgenes Farm.
